ac.2: Every pair of positions is scored — even the ones softmax then mutes to almost zero. That is why the work grows with the square of the context.
ac.3: The causal mask lets position i see only 0…i, so there are n(n+1)/2 pairs instead of n². For Llama-3-8B at 8,192 tokens that is about 33.6 million scores per head and layer; with 32 heads and 32 layers it is roughly 34 billion numbers for a single prefill.
ac.4:
pairs/head/layer = n(n+1)/2   (causal)
                  = n²        (no mask)
per prefill       = pairs × 32 × 32
ac.5: Softmax skips nothing. The whole QKᵀ is computed and most weights simply come out very small. The model works out that a position does not matter instead of skipping it.
ac.6: Prefill — processing the whole prompt in one pass — is O(n²) in the number of tokens. One decode step, generating a single new token with the KV cache, is O(n): the new query is compared with every cached key. A whole generation is therefore still quadratic.
ac.8: FlashAttention computes exactly the same thing. It tiles the work with an online softmax, so the n×n matrix is never written to memory: memory becomes O(n), but the multiplications are still O(n²).
ac.9: GQA (several query heads share one K/V pair) and MQA (all query heads share a single pair) shrink the KV cache, and PagedAttention keeps that cache in fixed blocks. All three save memory; none changes which pairs are computed.
ac.11: Local window: a position sees only the latest W tokens, which gives O(nW). Gemma 3 uses roughly 5 local layers per global one, and gpt-oss alternates them. Information from far away still arrives indirectly through the global layers.
ac.12: Sparse attention with selection: a cheap indexer picks top-k positions and full attention runs only against those (for example DeepSeek DSA).
ac.13: Linear attention and state-space models (Mamba, hybrids) do no pairwise comparison at all: the history is compressed into a fixed-size state.
ac.14: This is why long context is expensive, and why many new models "cheat" in some of the layers. FlashAttention makes attention cheaper in memory, not in arithmetic.
